L38: ## RRAEH'S
L39: 
L40: ## ONCOLOGY SERVICES
L41: 
L42: Our oncology team provides compassionate, advanced cancer care for pets, including diagnostics, treatment, and palliative support by referral.
L43: ### NOTICE: Oncology Not Accepting New Patients At This Time
L44: 
L45: At this time, Red River Animal Emergency Hospital & Referral Center is not accepting new oncology patients.
L46: 
L47: We understand how important specialized cancer care is for your pet, and we are committed to helping you navigate the next steps. If you are seeking oncology services, please 【4†contact our team】 and we will gladly provide referrals to trusted providers in the region.
L48: We appreciate your understanding and hope to offer oncology services again in the near future. Please check back for updates.
L49: ### OFFERING
L50: # Pet Oncology Services in Fargo
L51: 
L52: At Red River Animal Emergency Hospital & Referral Center, we understand how overwhelming it can be to learn your pet has cancer. That’s why we are proud to provide advanced pet oncology services, offering both hope and compassionate care for dogs and cats.
L53: If your family veterinarian recommends oncology care, they can submit a referral directly through our online portal, or you can call us at 701-478-9299 for more information. And for emergencies, our hospital remains open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
L54: ### What Is Veterinary Oncology?
L55: 
L56: Veterinary oncology focuses on the diagnosis and treatment of cancer in pets. At RRAEH, this specialty care is provided by a board-certified veterinary oncologist who works closely with our surgery, internal medicine, imaging, and ICU teams to create complete treatment plans. This collaborative approach allows us to give your pet the highest level of care, combining expertise across multiple disciplines.
L57: ### What Cancers Are Most Common In Pets?
L58: 
L59: While cancer can affect any pet, some of the 【31†most common forms†www.germantownah.com】 include:
L60: 
L61:   * Lymphoma
L62:   * Mast cell tumors
L63:   * Osteosarcoma (bone cancer)
L64:   * Soft tissue sarcomas
L65:   * Mammary tumors
L66:   * Oral melanoma
L67:   * Transitional cell carcinoma (bladder cancer)
L68: 
L69: Each type of cancer requires careful evaluation and staging so we can recommend the most effective treatment options for your pet.
L70: ### How Are Pet Cancers Diagnosed?
L71: 
L72: Accurate diagnosis is the first step in creating a successful treatment plan. At RRAEH, we use a range of advanced diagnostic tools to evaluate each case, including:
L73:   * Biopsies and aspirates (tumor, lymph node, bone marrow)
L74:   * Imaging: digital X-rays, abdominal ultrasound, CT scan, GI endoscopy, rhinoscopy, and basic echocardiogram (with access to boarded radiologist review)
L75:   * Laboratory testing: CBC, chemistry panels, coagulation testing, and other specialty blood tests
L76:   * Molecular diagnostics: Flow Cytometry and PARR for lymphoma, BRAF testing for bladder cancer
L77: ### Do I Need A Referral To See A Veterinary Oncologist?
L78: 
L79: Yes. Oncology appointments at RRAEH are available only by referral, Tuesday through Thursday. To schedule, your family veterinarian can submit records through our referral portal, or you may call 701-478-9299 for guidance. This process ensures we have all the necessary history and diagnostics before your pet’s appointment.
L80: 
L81: ### What Cancer Treatments Are
L82: ## Available At RRAEH?
L83: 
L84: Our oncology team provides 【10†comprehensive treatment options】 tailored to each pet’s diagnosis and condition. Services include:
L85:   * Chemotherapy protocols designed for your pet’s specific cancer type
L86:   * Targeted therapy, including Palladia and Laverdia
L87:   * Immunotherapy, such as the Oncept melanoma vaccine and Gilvetmab checkpoint inhibitor
L88:   * Pain management and palliative care, including bisphosphonates for bone support
L89:   * End-of-life and hospice care, with a focus on comfort and dignity
L90: 
L91: Every treatment plan is created with compassion, clear communication, and the goal of maximizing your pet’s quality of life.
L92: #### How Much Does Pet Chemotherapy Cost?
L93: 
L94: The cost of pet chemotherapy varies depending on several factors:
L95: 
L96:   * Type of cancer
L97:   * Medications used
L98:   * Size of your pet
L99:   * Number of treatment sessions
L100:   * Required monitoring or additional diagnostics
L101: At RRAEH, we provide written estimates before beginning any treatment, and our pricing is consistent day and night. Our team will walk you through all options, helping you make informed decisions that fit your pet’s medical needs and your family’s circumstances.
L102: #### Why Choose Red River Animal Emergency Hospital & Referral Center For Your Pet’s Cancer Treatment?
L103: 
L104: Families across Fargo and the surrounding region choose RRAEH because we provide:
L105:   * Care from a board-certified veterinary oncologist with advanced training in cancer management
L106:   * Access to multi-slice CT imaging, an in-hospital Blood Bank, and ICU-level monitoring is not commonly available in general practices
L107:   * Seamless collaboration between oncology, surgery, internal medicine, imaging, and emergency care
L108:   * Consistent availability, with 24/7 support for urgent needs
L109: A 【7†trusted community presence since 2005】, with clear communication and partnership with family veterinarians
L110: ### Schedule Your Pet’s Oncology Consultation in Fargo
L111: 
L112: At Red River Animal Emergency Hospital & Referral Center, we are here to support pets and families facing cancer with expert oncology services, advanced diagnostics, and personalized treatment. If your pet needs specialty oncology care, please ask your veterinarian to submit a referral or call us today at 701-478-9299.
